activities.anchor: The label has a birthday and an author
activities.caption: true or false — the label under investigation
activities.name: mwLabelJudge

statements.s: Petrarch gave the dark-ages mood its shape in the 1330s; later historians hardened the mood into a name.
statements.why: The label has a birthday and an author — which is exactly why it can be investigated.

statements.s: The thousand years after Rome built the university, the castle, the cathedral, double-entry bookkeeping, mechanical clocks and eyeglasses.
statements.why: Hardly a long night — and one of those centuries produced the printing press that ended the medieval world from inside.

statements.s: Modern historians prefer Chris Wickham's framing: an age of darkness in which Rome's fragments were lost.
statements.why: Not darkness but inheritance: Rome's fragments were reassembled into three very different successor civilisations.

statements.s: The people who lived through those centuries would have recognised the label 'dark ages'.
statements.why: They were busy building — and weathering history's worst pandemic.

activities.caption: file each inheritance under its heir
activities.name: mwHeirsBuckets

config.prompt: Rome's three heirs — file each inheritance:

items.label: the Corpus Juris Civilis — Roman law codified under Justinian
Hagia Sophia's dome, the largest interior space on Earth for nearly a millennium
the House of Wisdom, paying translators to render Greek philosophy and medicine into Arabic
al-Khwārizmī's algebra — his name gives us 'algorithm'
Charlemagne's coronation in 800 — the west's bid to claim Rome's crown
bishops and monasteries keeping Roman administrative habits alive

config.why: Byzantium kept the empire, Islam kept and multiplied the learning — Baghdad became the world's intellectual capital — and the Latin west kept the church.

activities.caption: pair each rank with its side of the bargain
activities.name: mwFeudalMatch

config.prompt: The privatised-protection pyramid — pair each rank with its obligation:

pairs.right: grants estates (fiefs) to nobles, owed homage and knights in return
sub-grant downward in turn, owing the king knights and service
the era's tank — expensive to equip, trained from boyhood, nearly unstoppable in the open field
bound to the land but not owned by it; work the lord's fields for strips to feed themselves

config.why: Beneath feudalism's political ladder ran manorialism, the economic half — a pyramid of mutual obligations held together by oaths and land rather than by money, which had mostly vanished.

activities.anchor: the story runs in three acts
activities.caption: line up the papal crisis, earliest first
activities.name: mwPapalOrder

config.prompt: The late-medieval papal crisis — order the acts, earliest first:
items: Pope Boniface VIII clashes with Philip IV over taxing the clergy; mercenaries seize and rough up the ageing pope
the papal court settles at Avignon, just across the border of France — Petrarch's 'Babylonian Captivity of the Church'
the Great Schism: two rival popes from 1378 — and a council in 1409 produces three
the Council of Constance (1414–18) deposes all three and elects one
config.why: The office survived; the awe did not. A Church that had claimed supremacy over kings had been beaten by one, moved by another and split in three — the Reformation had its kindling.

activities.anchor: The one institution that reliably taught women to read
activities.caption: pair each named hand with her work
activities.name: mwScribesMatch

config.prompt: Named hands in an anonymous scriptorium — pair each with her work:

pairs.right: visions, medicine and philosophy — and more surviving liturgical chant than any other medieval composer
compiled the Hortus deliciarum, thought to be the first encyclopedia by a woman
signed herself 'paintress and helper of God'
drew herself inside a giant initial letter: 'Guda, a sinner, wrote and painted this book'

config.why: Vows usually barred signatures, so most illuminated manuscripts are anonymous — which makes the ones that carry names precious. Literacy had to be lived inside the walls.

activities.anchor: the plague was less an interruption of history than an editor of it
activities.caption: call the share — the four-year fall
activities.name: mwPlagueEstimate

config.prompt: Within four years of October 1347, roughly what share of Europe's population did the Black Death kill?
config.why: Between a third and half of Europe — and the crash is visible in any reconstruction: famine and plague erased a quarter of the total in half a century, one disease resetting eight centuries of growth.
config.context: Modern DNA work on plague pits has settled the pathogen debate: Yersinia pestis, carried from the Black Sea into Sicily by Genoese ships.

activities.anchor: The social consequences were paradoxical and profound
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the paradoxical aftermath
activities.name: mwConsequencesSpot

config.prompt: One line of this consequence summary is wrong — click it:
lines: Labour became scarce, so wages rose — English harvest labourers could demand double.
Governments panicked and froze wages by statute in 1351, helping trigger the Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
Serfdom withered in western Europe as peasants bargained or fled to towns, even as it hardened in the east.
The Hundred Years War proved that armoured knights could finally out-fight peasant archers.
Ottoman cannon breached Constantinople's Theodosian walls in 1453, sending Greek scholars west.
config.correction: It was the reverse: peasant archers with the longbow (Crécy, Agincourt) killed knights from three hundred paces — the feudal tank, out-technologied.
config.why: Faith shattered and reformed too — flagellants, pogroms, and a Church whose visibly failed intercessions faced the questions Luther would later weaponise.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — the flat-earth tale, corrected
activities.name: mwFlatCloze

config.text: Educated medieval Europeans knew the Earth was round: Greek geographers had measured its %%0%% long before, and Columbus's own arguments were about the %%1%% of the ocean — not the %%2%% of the planet. The flat-earth tale is a nineteenth-century invention.
config.hint: He underestimated how far around it was — he never doubted it was round.
